purpose: Verify Prime guest FST publication and trace why IOS work stops after initial DVD/USB setup.

fst_validation.meaning: The guest sees the original Prime FST bytes and indices. The earlier synthetic WiiCompiled FST had 241 entries and must not be used as Prime guest FST.

runtime_probe.runtime_observation: All eight resource descriptors completed, IOS handled initial STM/NAND/network/time and DI requests, and execution progressed into /dev/usb/oh1/57e/305. The IPC queue trace then showed zero outstanding work while requests continued to enqueue; no later IOS packet was submitted. Aurora prewarmed pipelines. No fatal error appeared before the harness stopped the process, and no game screen was observed.
runtime_probe.queue_semantics_source: Ghidra decompilation of RM3E01_00 FUN_8050441C: after enqueue/signal, hardware submission via PPCMSG/PPCCTRL is guarded by DAT_80679C50 > 0. FUN_805041B0 is the registered IPC interrupt handler and adjusts this counter/starts the next queue item.
runtime_probe.instrumentation: Temporary bounded [ipc-queue-trace] at the start of the FUN_8050441C outstanding-count branch in a generated shard. It is diagnostic only and may be overwritten by translator regeneration.

rejected_experiment.change: Called OS_HLE_DispatchPendingPrimeIpcInterrupt at the end of translated FUN_8050441C.
rejected_experiment.result: Rejected and removed. It caused different reentrant startup behavior; /dev/di returned ISFS_ENOENT (-106), a subsequent IOS ioctl submit was unsupported, and a CD000004 MMIO write fault occurred with no current CPU context. This does not validate interrupt delivery.
rejected_experiment.state: The injected call is absent from the generated shard; only queue tracing remains.

limits: The runtime still reads resources from the private research extraction; ISO-backed runtime loading is incomplete.
No first game screen is verified.
The cause of the IOS outstanding-count/worker stall is not yet proven; do not force a synthetic completion or skip USB initialization.
Generated shard instrumentation is not reproducible through translator inputs.
next: Trace the registered IPC handler and the guest worker's wake/resume path around the first /dev/usb/oh1/57e/305 open. Determine why interrupt/queue processing stops after earlier DI requests. Keep the failed end-of-routine interrupt injection rejected; do not force responses. Once queue progress is correct, implement only the observed IOS device requests and continue to frame submission.

diagnostics.tail_state: After the /dev/usb open request, command 1 and three command 7 requests were enqueued with outstanding=0; head remained 17 while tail advanced to 27, get=1, put=11. No subsequent IOS request packet or IPC handler trace appeared before the process was stopped.

latest_followup.interpretation: The registered IPC handler is invoked for earlier startup requests, including the DI clear-cover operations, but not after the queue reaches the USB initialization path. This narrows the stall to guest scheduling/IPC queue reactivation at that phase; the FST is no longer the blocker. The precise missing wake/interrupt transition is not yet identified.
